messages:
ana: FYI - after merging the "eager-bind-by-fingerprint" batching heuristic we see a big host-side tail on tiny requests (p95 +~40ms). GPU timelines unchanged.

ana: Quick numbers from today's smoke run (short prompts):
```
host_total_ms p50: 2.0  p95: 102 (+40)  p99: 148
parse+tokenize_ms p95: 26.3 (+22)
batching_bind_ms p95: 12.1 (new eager-bind path)
stream_writev_calls p95: 4 (baseline 1)
kvcache_lock_ms p95: 3.4 (contention spikes)
```

ben: eager-bind-by-fingerprint was supposed to reduce kernel warmup by pinning requests to a batch early. Looks like it's forcing extra serialization and blocking on kvcache locks. Any flamegraphs?

rachel: Flamegraph attached - top shows ingress.process -> header_sanitize_lowercase -> reserialize_meta -> eager_bind -> memmove + proto_unwrap -> token_adapter_legacy. Also a cluster where batch alloc holds a mutex while kvcache_lookup waits.

igor: Header sanitizer? We introduced a metadata canonicalization step to normalize tenant headers for routing. It was implemented as allocate-new-string lowercasing all keys. That can force reserialization for HTTP/2 and push small frames. Did sanitizer run inline?

ana: Yes it's inline in ingress to guarantee determinism before routing. It allocates new meta proto for every request and runs before fingerprinting. For tiny chat requests that extra allocate/serialize path ends up hitting ICU during tokenization because of legacy adapter selection.

ben: Also eager-bind tries to grab the batch slot synchronously and will flush partial batches if timers say "bind now". Combined with header reserialize, we get many small frames and lost writev coalescing. Strace shows multiple writev calls and extra open("/usr/lib/icu/...") on the slow runs.

rachel: kvcache_lock_ms is surprising - looks like eager-bind holds the batch mutex while doing a kvcache warm lookup to attach session keys. The lock scope grew. So both parse and lock contention add up.

sidecar-bot: rolled back CL fb3a2e (eager-bind-by-fingerprint) on canary at 10:42 UTC.

ana: After rollback p95 fell back to baseline within ~12m. Confirmed kvcache lock wait drops and writev coalesce returns. Regression scoped to host ingress work; not model.

igor: Proposed remediation steps:
- revert eager-bind until we can make bind non-blocking (async attach to batch slot)
- move header_sanitize_lowercase out of the critical path: do an in-place lowercase for ascii-only keys or async sanitize for others
- change serializer to reuse buffers (avoid new proto alloc per request) and add a small buffer pool for meta writes
- tighten kvcache locking: use optimistic read + shard locks to avoid long-held mutex during warm lookup
- enforce writev coalescing at the transport: only flush when either payload > 512B or explicit flush flag

ben: Also add a unit that simulates 1-10 token chat over http2/grpc with common tenant metadata shapes to catch reserialization regressions.

rachel: I'll prototype an in-place ascii-lowercase (fast path) and a pooled serializer. If we can avoid ICU & legacy token adapter decisions by routing to token_adapter_v3 for our common metadata shapes, that'd remove most of the extra cost.

perfbot: scheduling stateless-canary with eager-bind reverted and ascii-inline-sanitize enabled at 11:05 UTC; collecting 25m of traces.

igor: I'll follow up with a microbenchmark showing memmove counts before/after the pooled serializer and a lock-wait histogram for the kvcache. If the async bind wins we'll reintroduce it behind a canary flag.

ana: Great. Marking incident P1 for Hosted and P0 for Dedicated until the async-bind + serializer pool lands. Paste any traces in-thread. :thumbsup:
